bull.b: Sustained gross margins near the high 50s and strong operating margins provide durable profitability and pricing power. This margin profile funds R&D, capital allocation and buffers earnings through semiconductor cycles, supporting long-term cash generation and reinvestment.

Very low leverage and consistently attractive ROE give Teradyne financial flexibility to invest, return capital and withstand downturns. A conservative balance sheet reduces refinancing risk, supports optionality (e.g., $1B revolver) and underpins multi‑year strategic investments.

AI-related demand now composes a majority of revenue, driving record sales and validating Teradyne's wafer-to-AI strategy. Exposure to hyperscalers and merchant GPUs creates a durable TAM tailwind and increases the likelihood of sustained orders and midterm share gains across compute and memory testing.

bear.b: Revenue and ROE have shown large swings tied to semiconductor capex cycles; past material declines highlight booking sensitivity. Dependence on customers' capital spending creates durable volatility in revenue, complicating forecasting and potentially stressing cash flow during downcycles.

Management flagged a significant inventory build to support future sales. When coupled with historically inconsistent cash conversion, higher inventories can tie up cash, compress near-term free cash flow and magnify downside if customer ramps or qualification timing slip.

Ongoing memory-product margin headwinds can limit company-level gross-margin expansion despite strong AI demand. Persistent lower-margin memory mix may require higher OpEx to pursue new TAMs and compress sustainable operating-profit improvement over the medium term.
